title: Rolling host refresh with proactive KV prewarm and service contracts
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Overview:
Perform a rolling host refresh for Dedicated fleets that minimizes SLO perturbation by introducing time-boxed eviction slots, a lightweight service-contract mechanism to reserve throughput during maintenance, and a proactive KV prewarm protocol to avoid cold-cache tail latency. This ticket covers the orchestration logic, preheat heuristics, API for lease requests, and a gradual rollout plan across regions.

Goals:
- Maintain 99.9% request success and p95 latency within current SLOs during host refresh waves.
- Keep token throughput loss <5% per maintenance epoch for platinum/dedicated tenants.
- Reduce cold-KV miss tail events by 80% compared to current drains.

Success metrics (to be monitored on dashboard):
- Fleet-level p95 latency delta during maintenance windows (target < +8ms)
- Percent of requests served by warmed KV prefix (target > 85%)
- Scheduled maintenance completion rate within window (target > 98%)

Design notes / approach:
1) Eviction slots: allocate short-lived, pre-announced eviction slots that limit parallel host drains in a shard to keep aggregate throughput above a service contract threshold. Slots are advertised via controller and consumed by host agents.
2) Service contracts: lightweight reservation tokens a tenant can opt into to guarantee minimum throughput during scheduled maintenance (used for revenue-tiered SLAs). Contracts throttle non-contracted traffic when necessary.
3) KV prewarm protocol: once a host is selected for refresh, the controller signals a preheat phase where fast workers replay cached prefixes for active tenants to populate remote caches on target hosts or sibling warm nodes using sampled request traces. Preheat uses rate-limited background token streams to avoid storming.
4) Hedging & fallbacks: if prewarm misses exceed threshold, controller extends eviction slot or falls back to a compatible lower-capacity model variant to preserve latency SLO.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Aggressive prewarm increases cross-host network and I/O; we prefer rate-limited preheat to avoid affecting steady-state throughput.
- Reserving throughput for service contracts improves SLAs but reduces capacity for best-effort tenants; billing and quotas need coordination with product.
- Full KV migration (copying whole prefix sets) was rejected due to complexity and storage churn; we instead opt for sampled replay and opportunistic prefix replication.

Implementation checklist:
- Controller: eviction-slot allocator and slot lifecycle (allocate/extend/cancel).
- Host agent: slot acknowledgement, preheat worker, graceful drain hooks.
- API: POST /fleet/slots to create reservations; GET /fleet/slots for status.
- Monitoring: maintenance window dashboard, prewarm hit-rate panel, SLO regression alert.
- Runbook: automated rollback criteria and manual override steps.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/rolling-host-refresh-protocol
- Spec PR (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289
- Implementing branch (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/eviction-slots
- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.net/d/maintenance-waves/rolling-refresh-overview
- Billing note (drive): https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/service-contract-billing.md

Open questions / blockers:
- Product decision on whether service contracts are opt-in per-tenant or bucket-level (need PM sign-off).
- KMS/HSM policy for preheat metadata in Private deployments — security asked for review.
- Autoscaling interaction: how do slot reservations interact with autoscaler eviction policies? Need flow spec for tie-breakers.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary in staging: run waves against synthetic traffic with canary tenants (2/2025).
2) Region pilot: us-east-1 low-risk tenants opt-in (2/2025).
3) Gradual expansion with automated health checks and automatic rollback on SLO regression (target 3/2025).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: preheat storms causing increased latency for production traffic. Mitigation: rate limits, backpressure signals, preheat QoS, and canary-first rollout.
- Risk: tenant surprise over reduced best-effort capacity. Mitigation: pre-notification, quota adjustments, and dashboarding.

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize API shape & contract with Product (assignee: Jonah).
- Wire up preheat worker skeleton and simulate replay traffic in staging cluster.
- Create monitoring panels and synthetic checks for prewarm hit-rate.
